say: god won't give you more than you can handle
god will never give you more than you can handle
god doesn't give you more than you can bear
god won't give me more than i can handle
never gives you more than you can handle
never give me more than i can handle
god won't put more on you than you can bear
god doesn't give us more than we can handle
note: That's a common saying, but it isn't a Bible verse. The closest is 1 Corinthians 10:13, which is about temptation, not about suffering: it says God provides a way out so you can endure it. Elsewhere Paul says he was burdened far beyond his strength (2 Corinthians 1:8).

say: god helps those who help themselves
the lord helps those who help themselves
note: Not in the Bible. It's from Benjamin Franklin's Poor Richard's Almanack (and older Greek sources). The Bible tends to say the opposite: God helps those who can't help themselves (Psalm 34:18, Romans 5:6).

say: money is the root of all evil
note: Close, but the verse says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, not money itself. The difference matters.
Not in the Bible. It comes from a John Wesley sermon in the 1700s, and possibly older Hebrew proverbs. The Bible does talk about clean hands and a pure heart (Psalm 24:4), which is a different idea.

Not a Bible verse; it's a Persian proverb. The nearest biblical idea is 2 Corinthians 4:17, that present trouble is light and momentary compared with what's coming, and Psalm 30:5 about weeping lasting the night but joy coming in the morning.

say: when god closes a door he opens a window
god closes one door and opens another
note: Not in the Bible (it's usually traced to a 1600s Irish proverb, and The Sound of Music). The closest verse is Revelation 3:8, where Jesus tells a small church he has set before them an open door that no one can shut.

That's a poem from the 20th century, not Scripture. The image it draws on is biblical, though: Deuteronomy 1:31 says God carried Israel through the wilderness 'as a man carries his son,' and Isaiah 46:4 says 'I will carry you' even to old age.

Not a Bible verse. People are usually thinking of Romans 8:28, which says something narrower: that God works in all things for good, for those who love him. It doesn't say every event is good or has a tidy explanation.

say: the lord works in mysterious ways
note: Not in the Bible; it's from William Cowper's 1773 hymn 'God Moves in a Mysterious Way.' The idea comes from Isaiah 55:8-9: 'my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways.'

say: hate the sin love the sinner
love the sinner hate the sin
note: Not a Bible verse. It's usually attributed to Augustine or Gandhi. Jude 1:23 comes near it: have mercy on people while hating even the clothing stained by sin.
Not in the Bible (it's from a 1600s English writer). 1 Timothy 5:8 is the verse people connect it to: someone who doesn't provide for their own household 'has denied the faith.'

say: to thine own self be true
note: That's Shakespeare: Polonius in Hamlet, not the Bible.

say: spare the rod spoil the child
spare the rod and spoil the child
note: The exact wording is from a 1600s poem by Samuel Butler. The verse it paraphrases is Proverbs 13:24: 'One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him takes care to discipline him.'

say: the lion shall lie down with the lamb
lion lies down with the lamb
lion will lie down with the lamb
note: The verse actually says the wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; the lion is there too, eating straw with the ox. The lion-and-lamb pairing is a later shorthand.
Nearly right. Proverbs 16:18 says 'Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.'

say: the truth will set you free
the truth shall set you free
note: That's John 8:32. Worth reading the verse before it: the freedom is tied to remaining in Jesus' word.
Proverbs 27:17: 'Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.'

say: where two or three are gathered
two or three gathered in my name
note: Matthew 18:20. It's said in a passage about how a church handles a member who has wronged someone, which is why it mentions such a small number.

say: train a child in the way he should go
train up a child in the way
note: Proverbs 22:6. A proverb, meaning a general observation about how things usually go, not a guarantee about any particular child.
Matthew 17:20, and again in Matthew 21:21 and Mark 11:23. The mustard-seed image is about how small the faith can be, not how big.

say: by the skin of my teeth
note: Job 19:20. Job describing how little of him is left.
Genesis 1:3, the third verse of the Bible.
Deuteronomy 32:10, and also Psalm 17:8 and Zechariah 2:8. The 'apple' is the pupil, the part of the eye you most protect.
Mark 3:25 (also Matthew 12:25 and Luke 11:17). Lincoln borrowed it for his 1858 speech.
2 Timothy 4:7, Paul near the end of his life. 'Fight the good fight of faith' is also 1 Timothy 6:12.

say: all things work together for good
note: Romans 8:28. Note the second half: 'for those who love God, to those who are called according to his purpose.'

say: i can do all things through christ
all things through christ who strengthens me
i can do everything through him
note: Philippians 4:13. Read verses 11-12 first: Paul is talking about being content whether he has plenty or nothing, not about winning.

say: for god so loved the world
to everything there is a season
there is a time for everything
time to be born and a time to die
note: Ecclesiastes 3:1, the start of a list that runs through verse 8.

say: eye for eye tooth for tooth
note: Exodus 21:24 (also Leviticus 24:20 and Deuteronomy 19:21). It was a limit on retaliation, not a license for it, and Jesus takes it further in Matthew 5:38-39.
Daniel 5. A hand appears and writes on the wall during Belshazzar's feast; Daniel reads it as the end of his kingdom.
Matthew 5:41: 'Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.' A Roman soldier could legally make a civilian carry his pack one mile.
Isaiah 40:15: the nations are like a drop in a bucket.

say: no new thing under the sun

note: 2 Corinthians 12:7. Paul never says what the thorn was.

say: the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak
note: Matthew 26:41, to the disciples who fell asleep in Gethsemane.

say: do unto others as you would have them do unto you
note: Luke 6:31, and Matthew 7:12. The name 'golden rule' came much later.

say: judge not lest ye be judged
judge not that you be not judged
note: Matthew 7:1. Keep reading to verse 5: the point is to deal with your own faults before someone else's, not to never assess anything.
Leviticus 19:18 first; Jesus quotes it in Matthew 22:39 and Mark 12:31.
Luke 15:11-32. The word 'prodigal' isn't in the text; it means wasteful.
Luke 10:25-37. Jesus tells it in answer to 'who is my neighbor?'
Jonah 1:17. The text says 'a huge fish'; 'whale' comes from some English translations of Matthew 12:40.

say: our father who art in heaven
note: Matthew 6:9-13, with a shorter form in Luke 11:2-4.

say: blessed are the poor in spirit
note: Matthew 5:3-12, the opening of the Sermon on the Mount.

say: take no thought for the morrow
note: Matthew 6:34, the end of a passage that starts at verse 25 about birds and lilies.
Hebrews 12:1 ('run with perseverance the race marked out for us'), and Paul's own in 1 Corinthians 9:24 and 2 Timothy 4:7.

say: camel through the eye of a needle
rich man eye of a needle
love is patient love is kind
be still and know that i am god

note: Psalm 23:1. The World English Bible says 'Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.'

say: plans to prosper you and not to harm you
i know the plans i have for you
note: Jeremiah 29:11, written to exiles who would stay in Babylon for seventy years. Read verse 10 too.

say: ask and it will be given
knock and the door will be opened
the wages of sin is death
note: Romans 6:23. The second half is the point: 'but the free gift of God is eternal life.'

say: let he who is without sin cast the first stone
without sin cast the first stone
the meek shall inherit the earth

note: John 19:30, Jesus' last words on the cross in John's account.
John 11:35, the shortest verse in the Bible.

say: greater love has no one than this
lay down his life for his friends
the fear of the lord is the beginning of wisdom
fear of the lord is the beginning
note: Proverbs 9:10, and Psalm 111:10; Proverbs 1:7 says 'the beginning of knowledge.'
Matthew 2 never says how many wise men there were, only that they brought three gifts. They aren't called kings, and they arrived some time after the birth, at a house.
Genesis 3 says 'fruit,' never 'apple.' The apple is a later European tradition.

say: the road to hell is paved with good intentions
note: Not in the Bible; it's a proverb of uncertain origin, often credited to Samuel Johnson or Bernard of Clairvaux.

say: the eyes are the window to the soul
eyes are the window of the soul
note: Not a Bible verse, though Matthew 6:22 says 'The lamp of the body is the eye,' which is probably where people connect it.
The phrase itself isn't in the Bible, but the idea runs all through it; Psalm 103:19 and Isaiah 46:10 say it directly.
Not a Bible verse; it's a 20th-century slogan. Psalm 46:10 ('Be still, and know that I am God') and 1 Peter 5:7 are what people mean by it.

say: god never gives up on you
god will never give up on you
note: Not a verse as worded, but Philippians 1:6 comes close: 'he who began a good work in you will complete it.'

say: this is the day the lord has made
this is the day that the lord has made
rejoice and be glad in it
the lord giveth and the lord taketh away
the lord gives and the lord takes away
note: Job 1:21, Job's words after losing his children and everything he owned.

say: valley of the shadow of death
the lord is my light and my salvation
weeping may endure for a night
cast all your anxiety on him
cast all your cares upon him
come to me all you who are weary
come unto me all ye that labour
they that wait upon the lord
mount up with wings as eagles
fear not for i am with you
do not fear for i am with you
note: Isaiah 41:10; 'I am with you always' is Matthew 28:20.

say: trust in the lord with all your heart
lean not on your own understanding
lean not unto thine own understanding
thy word is a lamp unto my feet
the joy of the lord is your strength
joy of the lord is my strength
he who began a good work
will carry it on to completion
all have sinned and fall short
fall short of the glory of god
man shall not live by bread alone
children are a gift from the lord

note: Ephesians 5:22-33. Read the whole passage; verse 21 ('subjecting yourselves to one another') sets it up.
Genesis 2:24; Jesus quotes it in Matthew 19:5-6, which is where 'let no one separate' comes from.

say: honour thy father and thy mother
note: Exodus 20:12, the fifth commandment; Paul quotes it in Ephesians 6:2.

say: it is more blessed to give than to receive
note: Acts 20:35. Paul says Jesus said it; it doesn't appear in the Gospels.

say: the borrower is servant to the lender
borrower is slave to the lender
a good name is better than riches
good name rather than great riches
there your heart will be also

note: 1 Kings 19:12. The World English Bible renders it 'a still small voice'; some translations say 'a gentle whisper.'
1 Kings 19:12, Elijah on the mountain: not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice.
2 Samuel 1:19, David's lament for Saul and Jonathan.

say: a leopard cannot change its spots

note: James 5:11. Job in the book itself is more persistent than patient; the World English Bible says 'perseverance.'

say: i am the way the truth and the life
the way the truth and the life
in my father's house are many mansions
i go to prepare a place for you
wolf shall dwell with the lamb
there is no fear in love
god is our refuge and strength
a very present help in trouble
an ever present help in trouble
the lord bless you and keep you
the lord make his face shine upon you
what does the lord require of you
do justly love mercy walk humbly
act justly love mercy walk humbly

note: Exodus 3. Moses at Horeb, the bush that burns without burning up.
Genesis 37, and the rest of Joseph's story through chapter 50.

say: where you go i will go
for such a time as this
paul on the road to damascus

note: Luke 22:14-23; also Matthew 26, Mark 14, and 1 Corinthians 11:23-26.

say: built his house on the rock
unless i see the nail marks

note: Job 1-2, then the long conversation with his friends.

say: steadfast love of the lord never ceases
his mercies never come to an end
note: Lamentations 3:22-23. The World English Bible says 'loving kindnesses' where some translations say 'steadfast love' or 'mercies.'
